title: One Gunshot. Multiple Systems. How Integrations Coordinate Response.
summary: Discover how AmberBox integrations connect gunshot and threat detection with existing security systems to coordinate faster emergency response.
body_markdown:
Your security systems shouldn't operate independently when an emergency demands a coordinated response. Most large organizations have already invested in multiple security technologies. Access control manages entry. Cameras provide visibility. Emergency communications platforms distribute instructions. Security operations centers coordinate activity. The opportunity is to connect these capabilities so critical information can move across the organization immediately.


#### One Event Can Require Multiple Actions


Consider a gunshot inside a manufacturing facility. Security personnel need to know the precise location. Emergency responders need to be notified. Employees may need instructions. Visual indicators may be required in high-noise production areas. Each action serves a different purpose. But all of them begin with the same requirement:


#### Detection as the Starting Point


AmberBox provides real-time gunshot and threat detection designed to support a connected security environment. Its detectors identify supported threat events and provide location intelligence that security teams can use to initiate appropriate action. For confirmed gunshots, AmberBox automatically triggers security alerts, E911 calling, and direct communication with police dispatch. That initial detection can also provide a valuable trigger for connected security workflows.


#### Extending the Value of Existing Systems


AmberBox is vendor-agnostic and supports integration through an open API. This enables organizations to connect threat detection with other technologies within their security infrastructure. Depending on the configured integration, connected workflows may include: • Access control systems • Mass notification platforms • Visual alerts and strobe lights • Security operations and incident management workflows • Other connected emergency response technologies The objective is not to replace existing investments.It is to make them more effective by providing immediate threat intelligence.


#### Connected Response in Practice


A beverage distributor operating more than a dozen distribution centers integrated AmberBox with access control and strobe lights. When a detection event occurs, connected systems provide visual alerts and evacuation cues across the facility. This is particularly valuable in environments where machinery and ambient noise make audible instructions difficult to hear. The detection becomes the starting point for a coordinated facility response.


#### Security Works Better Together


An organization may have excellent individual security technologies. But during an emergency, the value comes from how effectively those technologies work together. AmberBox provides the detection intelligence, location information, and integration capabilities that help connect security infrastructure with emergency action. One detection. Multiple systems. A coordinated response.
